question: Which of the following is NOT correctly matched? [Pulicat — Location and Feature]
options: Pulicat — located north of Madras (Chennai) on the Coromandel Coast
Pulicat Lake — a brackish lagoon separating Pulicat from the open sea
Pulicat — the Dutch built Fort Geldria here in 1613
Pulicat — located in present-day Kerala, near Kozhikode
wrong_fact: Pulicat is NOT in Kerala. It is located on the Coromandel (East) Coast, straddling the border of present-day Andhra Pradesh and Tamil Nadu, north of Chennai. Kerala is on the Malabar (West) Coast.
explanation: Pulicat (Pazhaverkadu) is on the Coromandel Coast, north of Chennai, at the edge of the Pulicat Lake (a brackish lagoon). The Dutch built Fort Geldria there in 1613, making Pulicat their main base on the Coromandel Coast. It is in no way connected to Kerala or Kozhikode, which are on the opposite coast.

question: Which of the following is NOT correctly matched? [Pulicat — Dutch Fort and Trade]
options: Fort Geldria — Dutch fort built at Pulicat (1613)
Pulicat — served as VOC headquarters on the Coromandel Coast until 1690
Pulicat — major centre for weaving cotton textiles for export
Pulicat — headquarters of Dutch Coromandel shifted here from Nagapattinam
wrong_fact: The Dutch Coromandel headquarters was NOT shifted from Nagapattinam to Pulicat. Rather, after 1690, the Dutch headquarters on the Coromandel Coast was shifted FROM Pulicat TO Nagapattinam — the reverse of what is stated.
explanation: Fort Geldria was built at Pulicat in 1613. Pulicat served as the VOC's Coromandel headquarters until 1690. It was a thriving textile centre. However, in 1690, the Dutch headquarters was moved FROM Pulicat TO Nagapattinam — not the other way around. The option reverses the direction of the shift.

question: Which of the following is NOT correctly matched? [Pulicat — Rival European Presence and Conflicts]
options: English factory near Pulicat — established at Armagaon (Armagon) in 1626
Danish presence near Pulicat — Danish fort at Tranquebar (Tharangambadi), 1620
Portuguese expelled from Pulicat — by the Dutch in 1610
French established their rival settlement — at Pondicherry, south of Pulicat
wrong_fact: The Portuguese did not have a strong fort at Pulicat that was expelled in 1610. Pulicat was largely a Dutch establishment from 1609 onwards. The Dutch captured the Portuguese fort at Pulicat in 1609 (not 1610), but the framing 'Portuguese expelled from Pulicat by Dutch in 1610' misrepresents both the date and the nature of the conflict.
explanation: The English established their Coromandel factory at Armagaon (near Pulicat) in 1626. The Danish built their fort at Tranquebar in 1620. Pondicherry became the French settlement south of the Coromandel region. Regarding the Portuguese at Pulicat — the Dutch seized the Portuguese post at Pulicat in 1609, not 1610, making the year in the option incorrect.
